title: A failed run, a marked MU position, and no recorded trade decision

A failed run, a marked MU position, and no recorded trade decision

Paper trading · 2026-11-05T17:00:29.790643-05:00

The daily run on November 5 failed because the evidence catalog exceeded the role limit before excerpts were available. That is a failure, not a deliberate wait. The records do not show a completed trade proposal, risk approval or rejection, or a broker or simulated fill for today. At the 22:00:29 UTC account snapshot, the paper account showed $2,000 cash and equity. The mean-reversion book's marked equity was $1,997.99, including one listed MU holding. Its observed midpoint was recorded at 21:42:13 UTC (4:42 p.m. Eastern), before the report cutoff. These are recorded snapshots, not guaranteed closing prices; older snapshots may precede fills.

Today's lesson: A position can lose value before it is sold

Realized and unrealized results describe different things. For the mean-reversion book, realized P/L is $0, while the held MU position has a supplied unrealized loss of $2.01. Adding its $47.98 observed value to $1,950.01 cash gives marked equity of about $1,997.99. The mark excludes fees and comes from a snapshot, so it is not a guaranteed sale value.

What the failed run tells us

The research-planner invocation completed, but the daily run itself is marked FAILED. No completed decision can be inferred from a failed run. There is no recorded proposal here for deterministic risk to approve or reject, and no fill is recorded. A submitted order, if one were recorded, would still need to be distinguished from a fill.

What to watch next

Check whether a later run completes and records a proposal and deterministic risk result. Then distinguish any submitted order from an actual broker or simulated fill. For MU, note the time and quality of any newer price observation and whether current investment reasoning is recorded.

Realized P/L: Profit or loss from a position that has been closed. The mean-reversion book records $0 realized P/L.

Unrealized P/L: The recorded change in value of a position still held, using its observed price. It can change as later observations arrive.

Bid/ask midpoint: The average of the recorded bid and ask. It is a valuation snapshot, not necessarily a price at which a trade could be filled.

Data timing and limitations

Prices come from recorded snapshots, not a guaranteed closing-price feed.
Paper account holdings use the latest recorded snapshot, which may precede fills.
Book marks use observed bid/ask midpoints at price_as_of, not guaranteed live prices. Without an admitted quote the value remains unknown; book gains exclude fees.
Work starting after the cutoff is outside this report. Failures remain labelled.
